# For the AI working on this suite

This is a Java 17 + Maven + Playwright + JUnit 5 test suite for **https://playwright-playground.com**, generated by Suite
Builder from a crawl of the site. You are most likely here to turn a **user story** (and pages the
user saved from their browser) into **tests that read like the story**, so that someone who does
not code can follow what a test does without comments.

## Off limits: the suite's rules

SuiteRules.java, SuiteRulesTest.java, HarnessTest.java, SUITE-RULES.md and `src/test/resources/suite-rules/fingerprints.txt` test the
tests; edit none of them, and never skip SuiteRulesTest. A hard or story rule broken means the test (or
the story) is what is wrong; an advisory one is a warning. Edit inside YOURS blocks; regenerating keeps
them. A rule you think wrong: say so to the person.

**secrets/** holds the accounts signed-in tests use (secrets/README.md): never read, print, copy or list a file
there (search and list from src/ or the folder you need, never the whole suite), and never write an
account into code. Run signed-in tests; ask the person to fill in an account.

## Pages read signed in

A page class named for a role (`AccountAsUserPage`) is a page the crawl read signed in as that role. A test
of it signs in first, as its role: `signInAs("user");`, then the chain as any other test. The account comes
from the environment, Suite Builder's store when the suite is docked, or secrets/user.login (core/Credentials);
each role's sign-in page is in pages/signin. A test with no account fails at once, saying where to put one.

## How this project tells you things

You do not need to read everything. Context sits next to what it describes:

- **Every file's first lines give its EDIT RULES.** Most files are generated, with **YOURS** blocks:
  ```java
  // ==== YOURS (elements): safe to edit; regenerating keeps what is between these lines ====
  // ==== END YOURS (elements) ====
  ```
  Write only inside YOURS blocks, or in files you create. Everything outside them is rewritten
  the next time the suite is regenerated from a new crawl. A file marked "this whole file is
  yours" is never overwritten. Never remove the marker lines themselves.
- **Every page class's Javadoc** says what the page is, the words a story may use for it, how a
  test gets there, what the crawl saw on it, and whether it has a form.
- **Every Elements constant** says where the crawl saw it.
- **Every package has a package-info.java** saying what belongs there.
- **ai/GLOSSARY.md** maps the words of a story ("Careers", "the Services menu") to page classes and
  the method that gets there. Start there.
- **controls/** lists, for each page type, the buttons, fields and dropdowns the crawl saw, each
  with the words a story may use for it and a line to paste into the page's Elements enum
  (controls/HomePage.md; controls/Everywhere.md for ones on most pages). Look there
  before asking the user for a saved page.
- **stories/** is the story inbox: people drop plain-text stories into stories/new/;
  stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md says how to implement each one, or push back on it.
- **ai/recipes/** holds short how-tos; read the one a task needs. **ai/API.md** lists every library method, with its parameters.
- **KNOWN-ISSUES.md** lists failures that are the site's fault, not the suite's. Do not "fix" them.
- **crawl/** holds the crawl itself (playwright-playground.com.crawl.json, playwright-playground.com.templates.json) for details no class has.
  **crawl/pages/** has each page read, as the crawl saw it (its HTML: find elements there, and check
  a locator with `suite locate playwright-playground-com-tests <page> "<locator>"` where Suite Builder is installed).

## From a story to a test

Stories to do are files in stories/new/: stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md decides, for each, whether to
implement it (the steps below) or push back, and what to do with the file afterwards.

1. **Find the pages.** Look the story's words up in ai/GLOSSARY.md; read those page classes.
2. **Match saved pages to classes.** The user saves pages to `saved-pages/<PageClass>/` (see
   saved-pages/README.md). A saved page that fits no class is a page the crawl did not read:
   ai/recipes/add-a-page-type.md.
3. **Add the elements** the story needs to that page's Elements enum, in its YOURS block:
   ai/recipes/add-an-element.md. Look them up in controls/ first (a line to paste for each
   button and field the crawl saw); otherwise take locators from the saved page, never guess them.
4. **Add the actions and checks** the story needs, named for what a visitor does or sees, in
   the YOURS blocks of the page's action classes, built from `UserActions` and `Checks` (ai/API.md lists them; Playwright itself where they lack what the story needs):
   ai/recipes/add-an-action.md. A sequence the story names ("sign up") is a task:
   ai/recipes/add-a-task.md.
5. **Write the test** in `src/test/java/com/playwrightplayground/tests/cases/`: ai/recipes/write-a-story-test.md.
6. **Check your work** (below), then add a line to CHANGES.md. Something the site does wrong goes
   in KNOWN-ISSUES.md, and is reported to the user, not worked around.

When a story needs something no saved page shows (what happens after a form is sent, a page
behind a login), ask the user to save that page. Do not invent selectors, URLs or texts.

## How a test must read

```java
package com.playwrightplayground.tests.cases;

import com.playwrightplayground.tests.Story;
import com.playwrightplayground.tests.StoryTest;
import com.playwrightplayground.tests.pages.home.HomePage;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.DisplayName;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

@Story(value = "PROJ-1", title = "A visitor can open Buttons from the header")
class PROJ1 extends StoryTest {

    @Test
    @DisplayName("A visitor can open Buttons from the header")
    void story() {
        new HomePage(page).open()
                .navigateTo().buttons()
                .verify().isLoaded();
    }
}
```

- One story, one class named after its id (`PROJ-1` is `PROJ1`, `engi-101` is `Engi101`), one `@Test`: one chain of page methods
  ending in one `verify()`, the story's outcome. Every method name says what a visitor does or sees.
- No Playwright calls, locators, waits or `Thread.sleep` in a test: those live in the page's
  actions. No comments needed: if a test needs one, a method is badly named.
- Expected texts are plain strings, never regular expressions.
- `@DisplayName` is the story's title; `@Story` is its id in the team's tracker.
- Element constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE, ending in what the thing is: `_BUTTON`, `_LINK`, `_INPUT`,
  `_SELECT`, `_CHECKBOX`, `_RADIO`, `_HEADING`, `_TEXT`, `_IMAGE`, `_MENU`, `_DIALOG`, `_FRAME`.
  Steps name them from that: `EMAIL_INPUT` is "the email input".

A run prints each step as a sentence, and a failure says which step failed and why:

```
-> PROJ1: A visitor can open Buttons from the header
   story PROJ-1: A visitor can open Buttons from the header
   1. Open the home page (/)
   ...
   FAILED at step 2: ...
   because: ...
```

## The library (com.playwrightplayground.tests.core)

| Class | What it gives you |
| --- | --- |
| `UserActions` | what a visitor does: click, hover, type, typeSecret, clear, choose, tick, untick, pressKey, readText, clickOpeningNewTab. Each logs its step. |
| `Checks` | what a test expects: isShown, isNotShown, allShown, hasText, hasValue (what a field holds), containsText, pageShowsText, hasCount (how many are shown, from the locator of all of them), isEnabled, isDisabled, isChecked, isNotChecked, hasAttribute, isOnPath, titleIs. Each logs its step and fails in plain English. `assume(met, why)` skips a test whose data is not there, saying why. |
| `WaitActions` | the waits pages are built from: for a URL, the page load, a title, an element to show or to go away, any condition (`until`). Never sleep. |
| `Headings` | `Headings.named(page, "Contact Us")`: a visible heading by its whole text, even when part of it is in a child element (`Contact <strong>Us</strong>`). Use it for heading elements. |
| `StepLog` | the plain-English log. `StepLog.step("...")` for a step no library call covers. |
| `SiteConfig` | where the site is (`-DbaseUrl`), `secret("password")` and `value("name", "default")` for data that must not be written into code. |
| `TestData` | the team's data, CSV in `src/test/resources/data/` (its README.md): `reusable("file.csv")` rows any test may read, `consumable("file.csv")` a row a test uses up; `-Denvironment=staging` reads data/staging/ first. |
| `LoadablePage` | base of every page class: `get()` waits until the page has fully loaded or throws, saying what was not ready. |

A page has the doors it needs, each a class of its own (`read()`, `verify()`, `navigateTo()` on every
page; `click()`, `enter()`, `check()`, `execute()` where it has something for them; ai/API.md lists
them): to add one, ai/recipes/add-an-action.md. A generated test never types into a form or sends it:
a form's test checks it is there and empty, and that the browser will not send a required field empty.

## Check your work

```
mvn -o -q test-compile                               it compiles (offline: no network needed)
mvn -o test -Dtest=SuiteRulesTest                    it follows the suite's rules (no browser needed)
mvn test -Dtest=PROJ1,SuiteRulesTest                 your story (PROJ-1) passes in a browser
mvn test -Dtest=PROJ1 -Dheaded=true                  watch it, half a second per action
mvn test -Dgroups=smoke                              every page type still loads
```

Run the first two before you report (offline, no browser); if you cannot run the browser ones, say so
and give the user those commands. Do not say a test passes unless it ran.

**SuiteRulesTest** runs last in every `mvn test` and checks the suite's rules (SUITE-RULES.md: each
rule, its tier, why). A failure says where, why, and what to write instead: do exactly that, and clear
the advisory warnings (`target/rules-report.md`) too.

**When a test fails**, the framework has already saved its evidence (nothing to add to a test for
it): `target/failures/<TestClass>/<test>/` holds `steps.txt` (the steps, the failed one marked,
the error, URL and title), `screenshot.png`, `page.html` (the DOM), `console.txt`, `network.txt`,
`run.txt` and `trace.zip` (open at https://trace.playwright.dev). Read `steps.txt` first; then
fix-a-failing-test.md. Only the latest run is in `target/failures/`; the run before it is in
`target/failures-previous/`.

## Safety

- **The live site is real.** A test that sends a form, orders, signs up or emails someone does it
  for real. Ask before writing one, and point it at a test copy: `-DbaseUrl=https://staging...`.
  See ai/recipes/forms-and-test-data.md.
- **Secrets never go into code**, a saved page or a log: `SiteConfig.secret("password")` and
  `UserActions.typeSecret(...)`.
- **Saved pages can hold personal data** (names, addresses, order numbers). Never copy it into
  tests or code; make up values of the same shape.

## What the crawl could and could not see

The crawl started at https://playwright-playground.com/ and read 41 pages.
It follows links only, logged out, and never sends a form: anything behind a login, a button that
is not a link, or a form's result is unknown to this suite until someone saves that page.

Not read: 2 sign-in and account pages (public pages only); 1 files (PDFs, images); 2 disallowed by robots.txt. Details: crawl/README.md.
